title: AI Gives 19% Less Diverse Answers than Web Searches
paragraphs: AI can quickly answer questions on any topic, but it might not give us the complete picture.
In fact, research published on arXiv has found that AI actually gives a narrower range of information compared with regular web searches.

Researchers tested 27 different large language models (LLMs), which are the systems that AI chatbots run on. They asked the LLMs questions about 155 topics, using 200 different prompts for each one based on questions from real users.
Then the researchers compared these responses to the top 40 regular Google search results for each topic.

The study included a wide range of topics that are often subject to debate, such as free speech and democracy. It also included questions on public figures from countries like the US, Russia and Saudi Arabia.

The researchers found that all of the LLMs gave a narrower range of information on each topic than a regular Google search did. Google was almost 19% more varied than even the best-performing AI, ChatGPT's GPT-5.

The researchers say this gap is in part due to how LLMs work — they compress huge amounts of text and repeat the most common patterns. Information that doesn't fit those patterns often gets left out of their answers.
Researcher Isabelle Augenstein from the University of Copenhagen explained why this is a problem, saying, "We risk exposing people to fewer perspectives and a narrower range of knowledge."
The issue may get worse if LLMs become increasingly trained on text that's been produced by other AI models, as the researchers believe will happen.
If AI is learning from already less diverse content, the range of information it gives will become narrower and narrower — causing what the researchers call a "knowledge collapse."
